clue.text: Final-year student of distinction securing a degree at university

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: grand means distinguished, of distinction

explanation.surface: A top final-year student is about to collect a university degree with honours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of distinction' reads as praise for the student but supplies the outer word; 'at' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A graduand is someone who has finished their studies and is waiting to be formally awarded the degree.

clue.text: Pasta dish — put port on it after cooking —

parts.note: Riga is the Latvian capital and Baltic port

indicators.note: cooking means messing with, so the letters of on it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A recipe for pasta: pour some port on it once it is cooked.
explanation.walkthrough: 'port' looks like the drink but is the Baltic port RIGA; ONIT cooked becomes TONI. 'put' is a link. The dashes run on into 3 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: Rigatoni is a type of pasta made as short ridged tubes, served as a dish.

clue.text: — and salad cream on cheaper variety of rocket?

parts.note: salad cream is a dressing for salad
prices that are down are cheaper

explanation.surface: Following the pasta of 2 Down, salad cream poured over a bargain bag of rocket leaves.
explanation.walkthrough: Rocket looks like the salad leaf, but a rocket is a severe telling-off; 'and' and 'on' are links continuing the clue from 2 Down.
explanation.definitionFit: A rocket is British slang for a severe reprimand, and a dressing-down is a scolding of the same kind, with a question mark for the playful sense.

clue.text: Road reconstructed about alternate parts of Aachen?

indicators.note: reconstructed means rebuilt in a new form, so the letters of about are rearranged
alternate letters of Aachen are taken, the second, fourth and sixth

explanation.surface: A road around Aachen in Germany is being rebuilt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is rearranged into AUTOB, and 'alternate parts of' takes A, H and N from AACHEN.
explanation.definitionFit: An autobahn is a German motorway, a kind of road.

clue.text: Plant left on yard wrapped in newspaper

indicators.note: something wrapped in another thing sits inside it, so the newspaper goes round

parts.note: a daily is a newspaper published every day

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the letter for left follows the letter for yard

explanation.surface: Someone leaves a plant on a yard, wrapped in old newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: In a Times across-style reading, 'left on yard' puts left after yard; 'wrapped in' then sets that pair inside the paper.
explanation.definitionFit: The daylily is a garden plant whose flowers last a single day.

clue.text: Chap with a lawyer's look?

parts.note: a DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer
mien is a person's look or bearing

explanation.surface: A man who looks every inch a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with a' links the man to his pieces; DA is the American public prosecutor.
explanation.definitionFit: Damien is a man's first name, so it can stand for a chap.

clue.text: Muse about fuel going up

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: oil is a fuel

explanation.surface: A thoughtful person reflects on rising fuel prices.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muse' looks like a verb for pondering; it is the noun, one of the nine Muses. OIL turned up reads LIO.
explanation.definitionFit: Clio is the Muse of history in Greek mythology.

clue.text: Company run on fixed lines stays involved in this

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
set means fixed, settled
RY, for railway, gives lines in crosswords

explanation.surface: A firm run on rigid lines keeps its staff involved.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stays' looks like a verb but means the stiff bones of a corset; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Corsetry is the making of corsets, which are stiffened with stays, so stays are part of this craft.

clue.text: Kepi's extremely unusual, worn by a commanding officer in Mexican location

indicators.note: a thing worn by someone sits on or around them, so the cap goes inside the officer

parts.note: a kepi is a peaked military cap

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken from unusual

explanation.surface: A soldier in Mexico is spotted in an odd kepi worn by the officer in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of 'unusual', U and L; 'worn by' sets the headgear inside the officer phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Acapulco is a resort city on Mexico's Pacific coast, so a place in Mexico.

clue.text: Conger eel regularly viewed as monster

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every second letter of conger eel is kept

explanation.surface: A conger eel is often thought of as a fearsome sea monster.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of CONGER EEL gives the answer; 'viewed as' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: In folk tales an ogre is a giant, man-eating monster.

clue.text: They may inform police about posse looting

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Informants tell the police about a gang that has been out looting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like it means 'concerning', but it rearranges the twelve letters of POSSE LOOTING.
explanation.definitionFit: Stool pigeons are informers, people who give the police information about criminals.

clue.text: At the end of the day, this could be a learning experience

definitions.text: At the end of the day, this could be a learning experience

parts.words: At the end of the day, this could be a learning experience
parts.note: the cliche phrase at the end of the day is taken literally: a lesson held after work, in the late hours

explanation.surface: In the end, everything is something to learn from.
explanation.definitionFit: Lessons held for adults after work hours are a staple of further education.

clue.text: Woman's name, one commonly spoken of

indicators.note: spoken signals that the word is said aloud, and what we hear is the answer

parts.note: moniker is the common, informal word for a name: one (a name) commonly

explanation.surface: A girl's name that a lot of people mention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' stands for a name; 'commonly' says to use its slang form, a moniker, which sounds just like the girl's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Monica is a familiar female first name.

clue.text: Knight caught, in a way, by fate

indicators.note: in puts the letter for caught inside the word for a way

parts.note: a lane is a way or narrow road
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: A knight is captured, in some fashion, by destiny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only a link word joining the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Lancelot is the most famous knight of King Arthur's Round Table.

clue.text: Tackle the falsifying of votes in election

definitions.meaning: the ropes and pulleys of a ship, its gear

definitions.text: the falsifying of votes in election
definitions.meaning: fixing a vote so the result is dishonest

explanation.surface: Someone tackles the problem of vote fraud at an election.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's rigging is its tackle of ropes, and rigging an election means fixing its result dishonestly.

clue.text: Inclination to consume sorbet — cold confection

indicators.note: to consume is to eat up, so one word swallows the others

parts.note: a rake is a slope or incline, as of a stage
a sorbet is a water ice
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A craving to eat sorbet, a cold sweet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclination' looks like a desire; it is a slope, RAKE, which takes in ICE and C.
explanation.definitionFit: A rice cake is a light snack made of puffed rice, a kind of confection.

clue.text: Having several burns, perhaps, could make you jumpy

definitions.meaning: a burn is a stream, so a place with many springs that feed streams

explanation.surface: Being covered in burns might make anyone nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: A burn is a Scottish word for a stream; land with several springs feeding streams is springy in this joke sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground full of springs (sources of burns) is springy in a playful sense, and springy also means bouncy or jumpy.

clue.text: Examination before the end of term

definitions.text: Examination before the end of term

parts.words: Examination before the end of term
parts.note: not a school test but a check-up during pregnancy, before the term ends in birth

explanation.surface: A test sat just before the school term finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Prenatal means before birth, so a prenatal check takes place before the full term of pregnancy is up.

clue.text: Where to find mobsters put to death (topped) in cell

indicators.note: in places the shortened execution word inside the cell

parts.note: a gland is a cell or organ that secretes

indicators.note: topped means its top, the first letter, is cut off

parts.note: to hang is to put to death

explanation.surface: Gangsters are executed in a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topped' removes the first letter, H; it also plays on the slang sense of killing, which suits the mobsters.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangland is the world of organised crime, where gangsters operate.

clue.text: Releases from commitment in very cold weather, we hear

indicators.note: we hear says the phrase is listened to, and its sound gives the answer

parts.note: a freeze-up is a spell of icy weather

explanation.surface: Getting out of obligations during a cold snap.
explanation.definitionFit: To free someone up is to release them from other commitments.

clue.text: Singer given a wave after Christmastide begins

indicators.note: after puts A and the wave behind the first piece
the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of Christmastide

parts.note: a roller is a long, heavy sea wave

explanation.surface: A singer gets a wave once the Christmas season starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A caroller is someone who sings carols, a singer at Christmas.

clue.text: Stanley Matthews, perhaps, taking position on field before goal

indicators.note: before puts the fielding position ahead of the goal

parts.note: leg is a fielding position on the leg side in cricket
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A football great takes up his place on the pitch in front of goal.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley Matthews was a celebrated English footballer of the 1940s and 50s; the field is a cricket field, not a football pitch. 'taking' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting great like Stanley Matthews is called a legend, and 'perhaps' shows he is an example.

clue.text: Motor needing to be repaired after middle bit's fallen out

indicators.note: something to be repaired is to be put back together differently, so the letters are rearranged
the middle letter of the seven-letter word needing is lost

explanation.surface: An engine needs mending after a central part has dropped out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'middle bit's fallen out' removes D from NEEDING, leaving NEEING, and 'to be repaired' rearranges that; 'Motor' looks like part of the surface but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine is a motor, the machine that drives a vehicle.

clue.text: Wild cheering completely engulfs a concert venue

indicators.note: to engulf is to swallow up, so the larger run takes in the letter A
wild signals the letters of cheering run riot into a new order

parts.note: all means completely, wholly

explanation.surface: Frenzied applause fills a concert hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' rearranges the eight letters as CRNEGIEH; 'engulfs' then puts A just after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: Carnegie Hall is a famous concert hall in New York City.

clue.text: Book — non-fiction, except for first part

indicators.note: except for means leaving out, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: the truth is what is not fiction

explanation.surface: A book that is factual except at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: TRUTH loses its first letter, T.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth is a book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Foreign team's Greek hero

definitions.meaning: the Amsterdam football club, a Dutch side
the strong warrior of Homer's Iliad

explanation.surface: An overseas side is named after a Greek warrior.
explanation.definitionFit: Ajax is a Dutch football club in Amsterdam and a Greek warrior of the Trojan War.

clue.text: Heard one guy and another perform in foreign capital

indicators.note: heard signals that the pieces are listened to, and the sound gives the answer

parts.note: cat is slang for a guy, a fellow; another guy is a man; to do is to perform

explanation.surface: Listening to two blokes performing in an overseas capital.
explanation.walkthrough: CAT, MAN and DO said together sound like the capital of Nepal.
explanation.definitionFit: Katmandu (Kathmandu) is the capital city of Nepal.

clue.text: Fence, one with blue and white exterior

indicators.note: an exterior is an outside, so the word for white goes round the others

parts.note: pale means whitish, white
I is the Roman numeral one
blue means sad, low in spirits

explanation.surface: A fence painted with blue in the middle and white round the outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' and 'and' are link words; the colours read as paint but supply the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a fence made of stakes set in a row.
